topic: The real Swedish deadline is January, not April
text:
Sweden runs two admissions rounds and they are not two chances at the same thing. The first opens in October and closes on 15 January; the second closes on 15 April. The second sounds like a comfortable fallback until you read what the authority says about it: many courses and programmes taught in English are no longer available for application in that round.

So for anyone applying from outside Sweden to an English-taught bachelor, the first round is the application and the second is a remainder sale. Supporting documents are due on 1 February, which is five months before the IB publishes results.
attribution: University Admissions, the national admissions authority, on its own key-dates page
whatThisIsNot: Not a claim that the second round is useless. It is genuinely open, and for a Swedish-taught programme or a late change of mind it is the right route.
